correctness.rationale: Code a vertex outside a pointwise named base by its binary adjacency vector; every vector occurs infinitely often, and each vector class is an orbit for graph automorphisms fixing the base. On a finite tuple the allowed edge changes are s_i+s_j+c over F2. Finite switches are realized by composing conjugates of a singleton switch, and complementation is realized by a complementing permutation; homogeneity then takes the transformed tuple to the target, so the composite fixes the base. A named pair excludes a pure complement, while three named vertices exclude any nonzero complement bit by summing the triangle equations. With switching only, the base bits are constant, and switching the new vertex gives the all-ones translation. With both operations and two named vertices, c=s_1+s_2 gives every translation on the two outside-edge bits. These cases give the stated table including the empty base; all outside orbits are infinite, and the m named points are the only algebraic types. It is the prefix through size three, not the single size-three row, that separates the groups. The archived bounded enumeration is consistent with, but not a substitute for, this argument.
